title: Solana developer glossary
lead: The words every Solana program lesson on Sol.College uses, in plain English, with a link to the official docs and to the live lessons that show each one in real code.

terms.name: Account
terms.def: Everything on Solana is an account: an address, a lamport balance, an owner program, and an optional data buffer. Programs themselves are accounts. Only the owner program can change an account's data.

terms.name: Program Derived Address (PDA)
terms.def: An address computed from seeds and a program ID that has no private key. Only that program can 'sign' for it, by passing the seeds into invoke_signed (Anchor: CpiContext::new_with_signer). Used so a program can own vaults, one account per user, or one account per (x, y).

terms.name: Seeds
terms.def: The bytes a PDA is computed from, for example b"escrow" and a wallet's 32-byte key. The same seeds always produce the same address. Each seed is at most 32 bytes.

terms.name: Bump seed
terms.def: The extra byte (usually found by counting down from 255) that pushes a PDA off the ed25519 curve so it has no private key. Programs store the canonical bump and pass it back when signing.

terms.name: init (Anchor)
terms.def: An account constraint that creates the account in the same instruction: it pays rent, assigns the program as owner, and writes the 8-byte discriminator. Combined with seeds, it also makes that address unique — a second init at the same seeds fails with 'already in use'.

terms.name: init_if_needed
terms.def: Like init, but succeeds if the account already exists. Use it with care: you must still validate the existing account, or an attacker can pass a different one that happens to be initialized.

terms.name: has_one
terms.def: An Anchor constraint: has_one = authority means account.authority must equal the account in the context named authority. Combined with authority: Signer, this is the standard way to require the stored authority to sign. If you forget it, any signer can be passed in that slot.

terms.name: constraint
terms.def: A boolean Anchor checks before the handler runs, for example constraint = maker.key() == bet.maker. Failure is ConstraintError (or your custom error with @). This is where most authorization belongs.

terms.name: Signer
terms.def: An account whose private key signed the transaction. Programs check this flag to authorize actions. A PDA cannot be a Signer in the usual sense; it 'signs' a CPI through invoke_signed.

terms.name: Payer
terms.def: The signer who pays the lamports to create a new account (its rent). In Anchor, payer = user on an init account.

terms.name: Owner
terms.def: The program that is allowed to change an account's data. System-owned accounts hold only lamports (wallets, and some vault PDAs). Program-owned accounts hold data, and only that program may move their lamports directly.

terms.name: Rent exemption
terms.def: An account must hold a minimum lamport balance proportional to its size or the network may garbage-collect it. Closing an account returns that rent to a chosen destination. Withdrawals that would dip below the rent floor are a common safety check.

terms.name: close (Anchor)
terms.def: close = destination marks an account to be closed at the end of the instruction: data is zeroed and its lamports (the rent) go to destination. Used after a vault is emptied so the account cannot be reused.

terms.name: Lamports
terms.def: The smallest unit of SOL: 1 SOL = 1,000,000,000 lamports. Instruction amounts are almost always u64 lamports, not SOL.

terms.name: System Program transfer
terms.def: The native way to move SOL: a CPI to the System Program. The source must sign (a wallet, or a PDA via invoke_signed). Any account may receive SOL, including one a program owns. A program-owned account with data cannot be the source of a System transfer — the program must edit lamports directly, or keep the money in a system-owned vault PDA.

terms.name: invoke_signed (PDA signing)
terms.def: The syscall that lets a program sign a CPI as one of its PDAs, by passing the PDA's seeds and bump. Anchor wraps this as CpiContext::new_with_signer. This is how a vault PDA sends SOL or tokens out.

terms.name: Cross-Program Invocation (CPI)
terms.def: One program calling an instruction on another — the Token Program to mint or transfer, the System Program to move SOL, Metaplex to create metadata. The caller passes the accounts the callee needs, and can attach a PDA signature.

terms.name: Clock sysvar
terms.def: A read-only system account at address SysvarC1ock… that holds the current slot and unix_timestamp. Programs call Clock::get() to enforce deadlines. The timestamp is not wall-clock precise, but it is the on-chain time every program agrees on.

terms.name: Sysvar
terms.def: A small set of reserved accounts the runtime keeps up to date: Clock, Rent, Instructions, and others. Programs read them; nobody else writes them.

terms.name: Associated Token Account (ATA)
terms.def: The canonical token account for a given wallet (or PDA) and mint, derived at seeds [owner, token_program, mint] under the Associated Token Program. Anyone can create it; there is only one per (owner, mint, token program).

terms.name: Mint account
terms.def: The account that defines a token: supply, decimals, mint authority, freeze authority. Minting requires a CPI signed by the mint authority, which can itself be a PDA.

terms.name: Token account
terms.def: An account holding a balance of one mint for one owner. Transfers are CPIs to the Token Program, authorized by the owner (or a delegate).

terms.name: Token Program (SPL)
terms.def: The standard program for fungible and non-fungible tokens on Solana. Token-2022 is a separate program with the same core layout plus optional extensions. Code must pass the right program ID for the mint it handles.

terms.name: Metaplex metadata
terms.def: The usual way an NFT or token gets a name, symbol and URI: a metadata account at PDA ["metadata", metadata_program, mint], created by a CPI to the Metaplex Token Metadata program.

terms.name: NFT (1-of-1 token)
terms.def: On Solana, typically an SPL token with supply 1, decimals 0, a frozen mint authority, and a Metaplex metadata account. The 'NFT' is the combination of the mint, its one token account, and the metadata.

terms.name: Account discriminator
terms.def: The first 8 bytes Anchor writes into each account it creates, a hash of the account type's name. It stops one kind of account being passed off as another. When you read raw account data, skip those 8 bytes to get to your fields.

terms.name: Checked arithmetic / overflow
terms.def: In a Solana program, wrapping u64 math can mint tokens or drain vaults. Use checked_add, saturating_sub, or a crate with overflow-checks = true, and write tests that hit the limits.

terms.name: Leftover / remaining accounts
terms.def: Accounts a client can append after the ones in the Accounts struct. The program must validate every one it touches (owner, seeds, relationship to the instruction). Forgetting to is a classic authorization bug.

terms.name: realloc
terms.def: Changing an account's data length at runtime. The payer must top up rent if the account grows. Used when a list (for example of LPs) grows.

terms.name: Vault
terms.def: An account that holds SOL or tokens for a program. Two common designs: a system-owned PDA that holds only lamports and signs transfers with its seeds; or a program-owned account whose own lamports (or token account) are the pot.

terms.name: Escrow
terms.def: A vault plus rules: funds stay locked until a condition (a deadline, a second signature, a judge's decision) is met, then they go to a named recipient. The program, not the frontend, enforces the rules.

terms.name: Multisig
terms.def: A vault that moves funds only after M of N named owners have approved a proposal. The program must tie every approval and the final execute to the same proposal and the same vault — leftover accounts that aren't checked break this.

terms.name: Threshold
terms.def: The number of approvals a multisig or a vote needs before an action executes. Stored on the account and compared at execute time.

terms.name: On-chain voting
terms.def: A proposal account, a voting period (usually from the Clock), and a rule for who may vote and with what weight (one wallet, one token, staked weight). Finalization should be permissionless once the period ends, or gated to a named authority.

terms.name: Quorum
terms.def: A minimum turnout for a vote to count, for example 10% of registered voting power. If the program stores a percentage but compares it to a raw count, turnout of 10 wallets can 'pass' a 10% quorum — a bug several of our lessons show.

terms.name: Authority
terms.def: The pubkey stored on an account that is allowed to do privileged things: mint, revoke, resolve a market, finalize a vote. 'The authority must sign' is almost always a has_one constraint plus a Signer.

terms.name: Staking (in a program)
terms.def: Locking tokens or SOL in a program vault in return for a receipt (a stake account, a gov token) and often a reward that grows with time. Unstaking may be instant or vest linearly. Distinct from Solana's native validator staking.

terms.name: Vesting
terms.def: Releasing locked tokens over time, usually linearly: withdrawable = total × elapsed / duration. The program uses Clock and must not let anyone withdraw more than earned, or restart the clock in a way that wipes a claim.

terms.name: Oracle
terms.def: A program that publishes a value (a price, a match result) other programs can read. Designs range from a single trusted key, to a stake-weighted average of many submitters, to a named judge. The quality of the value is only as good as who may write it.

terms.name: Bonding curve
terms.def: A formula that sets a token's price from how many have been sold, so anyone can always buy or sell against the pool, without an order book. The usual formula is constant-product (x × y = k).

terms.name: Constant-product AMM
terms.def: The curve token_out = reserve_token × sol_in / (reserve_sol + sol_in), which keeps the product of the two reserves constant. Each trade moves the price; a minimum_receive argument is the slippage guard.

terms.name: Slippage / minimum_receive
terms.def: The price may move between when a client simulates a swap and when it lands. The instruction takes a minimum amount the user will accept and reverts (ReturnAmountTooSmall, or similar) if the curve would pay less.

terms.name: Protocol / LP fee
terms.def: A fraction of each trade, in basis points (100 bps = 1%), taken for the team wallet, the liquidity providers, or both. The fee must actually move with the tokens or SOL — crediting a reserve without transferring the lamports is a bookkeeping bug our prediction-market lesson shows on devnet.

terms.name: Whitelist
terms.def: A list of pubkeys allowed to do something (trade, add liquidity). Usually a PDA with a Vec of members, checked with members.contains(&user). If the app has no screen to add members, only a script (or a later exercise) can.

terms.name: Transaction size limit
terms.def: A Solana transaction can be at most 1232 bytes. Instructions that create several accounts, write metadata and pass long strings can exceed this and never be sent. The fix is to split the work across two transactions.

terms.name: Event (Anchor emit)
terms.def: A structured log the program writes with emit!, visible in the transaction's program logs and to websocket subscribers. Frontends use events (for example PixelChanged) to update the UI without refetching every account.

terms.name: IDL
terms.def: The Interface Definition Language: a JSON description of a program's instructions and accounts that Anchor generates. Clients use it to encode instruction data and to know which accounts to pass. The IDL must match the deployed program.

terms.name: getProgramAccounts + memcmp
terms.def: The RPC call that returns every account a program owns, optionally filtered by data size or by bytes at a given offset (memcmp). Used to list all polls, all credentials for a student (offset 40, after the discriminator and a pubkey), and so on.

terms.name: View / simulate
terms.def: A way to call a program instruction that returns a value (Result<bool>, for example) without sending a transaction or paying a fee, by simulating it. Many apps just fetch the account and recompute the same boolean themselves.

terms.name: seeds::program
terms.def: An Anchor constraint that derives a PDA under a different program, most often the Associated Token Program, so the program can require the correct ATA without hard-coding its address.

terms.name: UncheckedAccount / AccountInfo
terms.def: An account Anchor does not deserialize or type-check. You must validate it in the handler (owner, key, relationship). Passing one as a payee without comparing it to a stored pubkey is how several of our lessons' bugs let the wrong wallet take the money.
